title: Spotting Phishing Red Flags in 30 Seconds
description: Learn the 3 instant indicators of email credential traps.
learningPoints: Check full sender email domain, not just the display name.
Hover over links to verify actual destination URL before clicking.
Be wary of manufactured urgency (e.g. 'account suspended in 15 mins').
question: An email from 'IT Support <support@secure-update-corp.com>' asks you to verify your password immediately to prevent account termination. What is the safest response?
options: Click the link and quickly verify credentials.
Reply asking if the email is legitimate.
Do not click anything; report the email as phishing immediately.
Forward the email to all coworkers to warn them.
correctAnswer: Do not click anything; report the email as phishing immediately.
explanation: IT never asks you to verify credentials via external links. Immediate reporting alerts the security team to quarantine the email enterprise-wide.

title: Password Vaults vs Plaintext Habits
description: Why password managers beat memory and sticky notes every time.
learningPoints: Reusing credentials across personal and work sites creates domino compromise.
Enterprise vaults generate 16+ character unique cryptographic passwords.
Never store passwords in notes, browser autofill, or spreadsheet files.
question: Where should your corporate passwords be securely stored?
options: In a password-protected Excel spreadsheet on your desktop.
In the approved enterprise password manager.
In your personal browser's built-in autofill tool.
On a handwritten note under your keyboard.
correctAnswer: In the approved enterprise password manager.
explanation: Enterprise vaults provide encrypted, auditable storage that resists browser-based infostealer malware.

title: Defeating MFA Fatigue Attacks
description: How to protect your second factor when flooded with prompts.
learningPoints: Attackers trigger repeated push notifications hoping you tap 'Approve' to stop the noise.
Never approve any push notification you did not immediately initiate.
Report spontaneous MFA floods to the SOC immediately.
question: At 2:00 AM you receive three consecutive MFA approval notifications on your phone that you did not initiate. What should you do?
options: Tap 'Approve' so the notifications stop buzzing.
Ignore it and go back to sleep.
Tap 'Deny' on all prompts and immediately alert Security via NETRAK.
Turn off your phone's Wi-Fi.
correctAnswer: Tap 'Deny' on all prompts and immediately alert Security via NETRAK.
explanation: An attacker with your password is attempting to push past your MFA. Denying and reporting prompts an immediate credential reset.

title: External File Sharing & Public Links
description: How anonymous links leak proprietary enterprise data.
learningPoints: Public 'anyone with link' shares can be indexed or forwarded indefinitely.
Always restrict shares to specified email addresses with expiration dates.
Default to 'View Only' permissions unless editing is strictly necessary.
question: You need to share a presentation draft with an external marketing contractor. How should you share it?
options: Create a public link with 'Anyone on the internet can view'.
Upload it to your personal Dropbox and text them the link.
Share from corporate cloud directly to their business email with an expiration date.
Email the file as an unencrypted ZIP attachment from your personal Gmail.
correctAnswer: Share from corporate cloud directly to their business email with an expiration date.
explanation: Direct recipient authentication and link expiry maintain access auditing and prevent runaway dissemination.

title: Safely Navigating Public Generative AI Tools
description: Protecting customer data and proprietary source code from LLM ingestion.
learningPoints: Public AI tools may ingest prompts into model training or persistent logs.
Never paste customer PII, confidential contracts, or internal code into free AI tools.
Use only corporate-approved AI platforms with enterprise zero-retention agreements.
question: Can you paste a customer database export into a free public AI tool to generate an executive summary?
options: Yes, as long as you delete the chat history afterwards.
No, pasting customer data into public AI services violates company privacy and data policies.
Yes, because public AI platforms encrypt all user inputs.
Yes, if you only paste 100 rows at a time.
correctAnswer: No, pasting customer data into public AI services violates company privacy and data policies.
explanation: Public AI tools lack corporate confidentiality guarantees and data deletion verification. Use enterprise-approved AI tools only.

title: Company Data Belongs in Corporate Cloud Tenants
description: The hidden risks of personal Google Drive and Dropbox syncing.
learningPoints: Personal cloud accounts bypass enterprise monitoring and discovery compliance.
If personal accounts are compromised, corporate data is exposed without IT awareness.
Keep work files strictly inside authenticated company tenants.
question: Why is syncing work files to a personal Google Drive account prohibited?
options: Personal Google Drive accounts run slower than enterprise servers.
It circumvents corporate data protection, monitoring, and legal compliance holds.
Google does not allow business files on personal tiers.
It fills up your personal storage too quickly.
correctAnswer: It circumvents corporate data protection, monitoring, and legal compliance holds.
explanation: Corporate Data Loss Prevention and access control cannot govern files once moved to unmanaged personal clouds.

title: Executive Impersonation (CEO Fraud & BEC)
description: Detecting high-urgency executive spoofing requests.
learningPoints: Attackers pretend to be executives in meetings needing urgent gift cards or wire transfers.
Verify unexpected financial or credential requests via out-of-band phone calls.
Legitimate executives never request iTunes/Amazon cards for vendor payments.
question: You get an urgent email from your CEO: 'I am in a board meeting, buy ten $100 gift cards right now and email the codes.' What should you do?
options: Purchase the gift cards immediately to avoid upsetting the CEO.
Reply to the email asking for confirmation.
Recognize the classic gift card scam, do not buy cards, and report the email.
Call an external store to verify gift card availability.
correctAnswer: Recognize the classic gift card scam, do not buy cards, and report the email.
explanation: Gift card demands are universally fraudulent Business Email Compromise tactics designed for untraceable financial extraction.

title: The Dangers of Found Flash Drives
description: Why you should never plug an unknown thumb drive into your PC.
learningPoints: Attackers drop 'bait' USB drives labeled 'Confidential Salaries' in parking lots and lobbies.
Plugging in a malicious drive can execute HID keystroke injectors (Rubber Ducky).
Hand all found or unknown media directly to IT Security.
question: You spot a 64GB USB drive labeled 'Executive Bonuses Q3' in the cafeteria. What should you do?
options: Plug it in to find the owner's resume or contact info.
Format the drive so you can reuse it safely.
Leave it untouched and alert IT Security or deliver it to the Security Desk.
Plug it into your personal laptop instead of your work PC.
correctAnswer: Leave it untouched and alert IT Security or deliver it to the Security Desk.
explanation: Malicious USB hardware can emulate keyboards to execute shell scripts in fractions of a second upon insertion.

title: Shadow IT & Free Online Utilities
description: Why unvetted browser extensions and converters pose serious risks.
learningPoints: Free web converters often store uploaded documents permanently on third-party servers.
Browser extensions can inspect and modify sensitive DOM data.
Install only tools available in the enterprise managed software portal.
question: You need to convert a confidential PDF to Word. Which approach complies with corporate policy?
options: Upload it to a free online PDF converter found on Google.
Install an unverified Chrome extension with 5-star reviews.
Use Adobe Acrobat Pro already licensed and deployed through the Corporate App Portal.
Send it to a free Discord bot to convert.
correctAnswer: Use Adobe Acrobat Pro already licensed and deployed through the Corporate App Portal.
explanation: Corporate software is vetted for data handling compliance; free web converters harvest uploaded confidential content.

title: Public Wi-Fi Hygiene: Always Tunnel
description: How to stay secure when working from airports, cafes, and hotels.
learningPoints: Unencrypted open networks allow local eavesdropping and man-in-the-middle attacks.
Rogue hotspots can spoof hotel or airport network names.
Always engage the corporate VPN before accessing work systems.
question: You connect to 'Airport_Free_WiFi' while traveling. What is your required next step?
options: Immediately open company email in incognito mode.
Connect to the corporate VPN before accessing any work tools.
Turn off your firewall to speed up the connection.
Browse only HTTP websites.
correctAnswer: Connect to the corporate VPN before accessing any work tools.
explanation: The corporate VPN encrypts all network packets from your laptop to corporate gateways, defeating local packet sniffing.

title: Protecting Corporate Hardware at Home
description: Physical security best practices outside the corporate office.
learningPoints: Lock your screen every time you step away, even at home.
Never allow family members or roommates to use corporate machines.
Secure home Wi-Fi with strong WPA3/WPA2 passwords.
question: Your roommate asks to borrow your company laptop for 10 minutes to print a boarding pass. What should you do?
options: Let them use it as long as you watch them.
Politely decline; corporate devices may only be operated by authorized employees.
Create a guest account on your work laptop for them.
Let them use it if you log out of Slack.
correctAnswer: Politely decline; corporate devices may only be operated by authorized employees.
explanation: Permitting third-party access violates non-disclosure and endpoint compliance agreements.

title: Mobile Device Security & MDM Profiles
description: Safeguarding company data on mobile devices.
learningPoints: Enroll in corporate MDM to enable containerized work profiles.
Never root or jailbreak a device that accesses corporate email.
Keep OS and apps updated to patch known mobile exploits.
question: Why are rooted or jailbroken smartphones banned from connecting to enterprise networks?
options: They consume too much cellular data.
Bypassing OS sandboxing allows malicious apps to intercept encrypted corporate secrets.
They cannot run company wallpapers.
They disable Bluetooth connectivity.
correctAnswer: Bypassing OS sandboxing allows malicious apps to intercept encrypted corporate secrets.
explanation: Jailbreaking strips foundational security barriers that isolate business applications from malware.

title: Defeating Vishing & Phone Pretexting
description: How to handle callers demanding internal employee info or credentials.
learningPoints: Attackers use urgency and caller ID spoofing to sound authoritative.
Never provide passwords, OTPs, or employee lists over the telephone.
Verify requester identity by hanging up and calling verified internal extensions.
question: A caller claims to be an auditor and requests the home address and payroll ID of three colleagues. What should you do?
options: Read out the information since they sound professional.
Refuse to provide personal employee data and report the vishing call to Security.
Ask them to send a screenshot of their badge before sharing.
Transfer the call to a junior colleague.
correctAnswer: Refuse to provide personal employee data and report the vishing call to Security.
explanation: PII and employee data cannot be disclosed over the phone without verified identity and legal authorization.

title: The First 15 Minutes of a Suspected Breach
description: Decisive steps to minimize damage when an accident happens.
learningPoints: Disconnect your device from Wi-Fi and wired network immediately.
Do NOT try to cover up mistakes; early reporting prevents widespread compromise.
Report the incident through NETRAK or the 24/7 Security Hotline.
question: You clicked an email link and typed your corporate password before realizing the site looked fake. What is your priority action?
options: Delete the email and pretend it did not happen.
Disconnect from the network and report the incident immediately in NETRAK.
Wait 24 hours to see if any strange logins occur.
Restart your laptop three times.
correctAnswer: Disconnect from the network and report the incident immediately in NETRAK.
explanation: Disconnecting halts active remote access while rapid reporting allows the SOC to revoke stolen sessions immediately.

title: Keeping Secrets Out of Public Git Repositories
description: How automated scanners scrape API keys within seconds of public commits.
learningPoints: Never hardcode secrets, private keys, or credentials into repository commits.
Use environment variables (.env) and secret vaults.
Keep all corporate repositories private under the enterprise organization.
question: You are writing a script that calls a cloud database. Where should the database password be stored?
options: Hardcoded as a string directly in main.ts.
In an unencrypted README file in the repository.
In a secure environment variable injected at runtime and excluded via .gitignore.
In the public commit message.
correctAnswer: In a secure environment variable injected at runtime and excluded via .gitignore.
explanation: Runtime environment injection keeps credentials out of version control and prevents public leakage.

title: What to Do When an API Key Is Committed
description: Emergency triage for exposed credentials.
learningPoints: Simply deleting the file in a new commit leaves the secret in Git history.
Immediately rotate and invalidate the key in the cloud provider console.
Report the incident so Security can audit access logs during the exposure window.
question: You pushed a commit containing an active production API key to GitHub. What is the most critical first step?
options: Push a second commit deleting the file.
Immediately revoke and rotate the API key in the provider console.
Make the repository private and do nothing else.
Wait until Monday to discuss it with your team.
correctAnswer: Immediately revoke and rotate the API key in the provider console.
explanation: Rotating the key invalidates the secret immediately, neutralizing any bots that harvested the key from Git history.

title: Handling Personally Identifiable Information (PII)
description: Complying with privacy mandates when handling customer records.
learningPoints: PII includes government IDs, health records, home addresses, and credit cards.
Only access PII on a strict business need-to-know basis.
Never export production PII into unencrypted spreadsheets.
question: A product manager asks you for a CSV dump of all customer home addresses and phone numbers to test a map feature. What should you provide?
options: An unencrypted production database dump via Slack.
Anonymized synthetic test data that contains no real customer identities.
A copy of the production database uploaded to Google Sheets.
The database credentials so they can query it directly.
correctAnswer: Anonymized synthetic test data that contains no real customer identities.
explanation: Synthetic mock data fulfills testing requirements without exposing real customer privacy to unauthorized environments.

title: Tailgating & Perimeter Awareness
description: Preventing unauthorized individuals from slipping through access doors.
learningPoints: Tailgating occurs when someone follows an authorized employee through a badge door.
Always ensure the door closes securely behind you.
Politely request that visitors badge in or escort them to reception.
question: A person holding coffee cups smiles and asks you to hold the secure office door open for them. What is the proper response?
options: Hold the door open to be polite and avoid conflict.
Politely inform them that company policy requires everyone to badge in, or direct them to reception.
Let them in if they are wearing business attire.
Give them your badge to swipe.
correctAnswer: Politely inform them that company policy requires everyone to badge in, or direct them to reception.
explanation: Polite firmness prevents social engineering intruders from bypassing electronic access logging.

title: High-Risk International Travel Protocols
description: Protecting digital devices when crossing international borders.
learningPoints: Notify IT Security 14 days before international business travel.
Use clean loaner travel hardware in high-risk foreign jurisdictions.
Never leave laptops unattended in foreign hotel rooms.
question: Why does IT Security issue loaner laptops for international travel to high-risk destinations?
options: To save airline baggage weight fees.
To ensure that primary production laptops containing proprietary IP are not seized or covertly cloned.
Because foreign electrical outlets destroy corporate batteries.
Loaner laptops are disposable.
correctAnswer: To ensure that primary production laptops containing proprietary IP are not seized or covertly cloned.
explanation: Loaner devices contain minimal data and can be wiped completely upon return, eliminating persistent firmware implants.

title: Securing Slack, Teams, & Digital Whiteboards
description: Avoiding accidental public disclosure in collaboration tools.
learningPoints: Ensure digital whiteboards (Miro, Figma) require organizational login.
Do not conduct business transactions in unapproved consumer apps like WhatsApp.
Periodically review guest channel memberships.
question: Can you invite external contractors to a public enterprise Slack channel where internal company roadmap discussions take place?
options: Yes, all channels are open to anyone with an invite.
No, external guests must only be added to dedicated single-channel guest spaces with approved scope.
Yes, if they promise not to read confidential messages.
Yes, Slack automatically hides confidential messages from guests.
correctAnswer: No, external guests must only be added to dedicated single-channel guest spaces with approved scope.
explanation: Unrestricted channel access gives third-party contractors visibility into unrelated proprietary business deliberations.
